slides.teacher_cue: The schwa is the most common vowel sound in English — and the most important to recognise. It is the unstressed, reduced vowel that appears in the unstressed syllables of multi-syllable words. Any vowel letter can make the schwa sound: a (about, balloon), e (system, problem), i (pencil, animal), o (lesson, button), u (support, circus). The schwa sounds like a very brief, neutral 'uh'. It is never stressed. Recognising the schwa explains why so many unstressed vowels are hard to spell — any vowel letter can produce it.
slides.expected_response: Students identify the schwa in unstressed syllables and understand that spelling must be memorised for schwa vowels.
slides.correction_move: Model: lesson — les/son. The o in -son is schwa. system — sys/tem. The e in -tem is schwa. button — but/ton. The o in -ton is schwa. Students identify the stressed and unstressed syllables and locate the schwa.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students trying to apply phoneme-grapheme rules to schwa syllables — explain that the schwa is the one sound where spelling must be memorised.
